_doc: DOD-M9C-SCREENBASE-1 — which attacks the DETERMINISTIC layer is answerable for.
layer1 = the attack carries something a rule can see: an instruction-override or
extraction phrase, a fake role/turn/system marker, or a disguise of one (encoding,
homoglyph, tag smuggling, leetspeak, cipher, ASCII art, structured-data or separator
injection). Missing one of these is OUR defect.
classifier = the attack is ordinary language whose harm is in what it MEANS: a
persuasive story or role-play frame, a many-shot or slow-escalation transcript, a
plausible email, a malicious tool description, adversarial gibberish suffixes. No rule
catches these without flagging ordinary conversation, so they belong to Layer 2 and are
reported separately, never as a deterministic-layer score.
Category names are bordair-multimodal's (payloads*/<category>). Assigned 2026-09-16 by
reading one payload per category; revisit when the catalog adds categories.
_mindgard_doc: Mindgard pairs an original attack with a disguised copy. The original's wording is not
ours to judge — half of it is jailbreak semantics. The DISGUISE is: if we flag the
original, we must still flag it disguised. The bench therefore scores Mindgard as
disguise robustness (caught-plain that survive the disguise), never as a catch rate.
These techniques rewrite characters, so a miss is a Layer-1 defect. The word-swap
techniques replace words with synonyms, which changes meaning, not form — classifier.
_p4rs_doc: P4RS3LT0NGV3 transforms. layer1 = the receiving model can still READ the output, so an
attack survives the disguise and we must see through it. unreadable = ciphers and symbol
alphabets the model cannot decode unaided; passing one is not a defect, and counting them
in either direction only flatters or punishes the score dishonestly.
